evals.prompt: Scaffold a new .NET Worker application solution named DemoApp with root namespace Acme, target framework net10.0, and the Minimal hosting pattern.
evals.expected_output: A worker-based scaffold with package versions resolved from NuGet, a generated Worker.cs file, and target-framework-aware test environment settings.
expectations: Recognizes the explicit Worker request and does not redundantly ask the user to restate app_host_types
Collects target_framework in addition to solution name, namespace, host type, and hosting pattern
Offers all active non-preview LTS and STS target framework quick picks before free text
Maps Worker host type to {AppType} = Worker
Includes Worker.cs in the generated worker project
Uses the current working directory as the scaffold root instead of creating a nested solution folder
Uses native structured inputs when available and a deterministic one-field-at-a-time plain-text fallback when they are not
Keeps package versions centralized in Directory.Packages.props instead of inlining Version attributes into generated project files
Keeps target-framework selection centralized in the generated root Directory.Build.props instead of adding TargetFramework directly to generated project files
Generates testenvironments.json instead of silently omitting the shared test environment asset
Names the generated solution file DemoApp.slnx instead of lowercasing it to demoapp.slnx
Still generates the solution file and functional test project even for a single-host Worker scaffold
Resolves worker package versions from NuGet instead of reusing stale remembered version numbers from prior runs

evals.prompt: Create a Web API solution named PaymentService under the root namespace Contoso using Startup hosting.
evals.expected_output: A web-family scaffold that selects the Web host type with the Web API variant, emits Api as the project suffix, uses the Startup pattern templates, and resolves package version placeholders before writing Directory.Packages.props.
expectations: Maps Web host type plus Web API variant to {AppType} = Api
Uses Program.startup.cs plus Startup.cs for the Startup pattern
Does not leave {LATEST} or unresolved *_VERSION placeholders in Directory.Packages.props
Keeps Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi aligned with the selected target framework major instead of always choosing the latest overall ASP.NET version
Does not ask for a second clarification if the prompt already says Web API
Writes the scaffold into the current folder rather than adding a PaymentService subfolder
Still generates PaymentService.slnx even though the scaffold only has one selected host type
Resolves package versions from NuGet instead of carrying hardcoded examples from a previous scaffold
Copies the complete shared asset inventory from assets/shared instead of cherry-picking only a subset of governance or dotfiles
Keeps TargetFramework centralized in the generated root Directory.Build.props instead of adding TargetFramework directly to generated app or test csproj files
Produces valid XML in generated root build props files before the first build rather than relying on mid-run repair
If it invokes scripts/resolve-package-versions.ps1, it does so through `pwsh -NoProfile -File` and never through `powershell` or `powershell.exe`

evals.prompt: Create a new MVC app named PortalSuite under the root namespace Fabrikam with the Minimal hosting pattern.
evals.expected_output: A web-family scaffold that selects the MVC variant, emits Mvc as the project suffix, and includes starter controller and view assets.
expectations: Maps Web host type plus MVC variant to {AppType} = Mvc
Generates MVC starter files including HomeController and Views/Home/Index.cshtml
Uses the Minimal hosting template for the MVC variant

evals.prompt: Scaffold a new Razor web app named TeamHub with root namespace Northwind and Startup hosting.
evals.expected_output: A web-family scaffold that selects the Web App / Razor variant, emits WebApp as the project suffix, and includes starter Razor Pages assets.
expectations: Maps Razor or web app wording to the Web App / Razor variant without unnecessary follow-up
Maps Web host type plus Web App / Razor variant to {AppType} = WebApp
Generates Razor starter files including Pages/Index.cshtml and Pages/Index.cshtml.cs

evals.prompt: Create a new .NET web solution named EdgePortal in the Acme namespace.
evals.expected_output: A web-family scaffold that asks for web_variant because the user requested a generic Web app, defaulting that follow-up to Web API.
expectations: Treats Web as the host family instead of a final variant label
Asks for web_variant when the prompt only says web
Defaults the web_variant choice to Web API

evals.prompt: Scaffold a solution with both Web and Worker host types for Acme Tools on net10.0, using the MVC variant for Web.
evals.expected_output: A multi-host scaffold with one MVC web-family project and one worker project, one functional test project per selected host type, and a README that lists concrete run commands instead of a single ambiguous placeholder.
expectations: Generates one web-family src project using the selected MVC variant and one worker src project
Generates one functional test project per selected host type
Rewrites the root README running section for multiple host types

evals.prompt: Create a new .NET web app named ForwardTrack and let me choose between the active LTS and STS target frameworks before scaffolding.
evals.expected_output: A web-family scaffold flow that presents every active non-preview LTS and STS target framework quick pick from the official releases index instead of reducing the choices to only the newest pair.
expectations: Offers the newest active LTS channel as the recommended target framework choice
Offers every other active LTS and STS channel as additional first-class quick-picks when they are supported
Still allows a custom target framework if the user does not want either quick-pick
Keeps framework-aligned ASP.NET package versions compatible with the selected target framework major

evals.prompt: Create an MVC site named MyMvc and keep the recommended root namespace if I do not type a custom value.
evals.expected_output: A scaffold flow that presents the solution name as the recommended root namespace and accepts that default without a second clarification loop when the user leaves the root namespace response blank.
expectations: Presents solution_name as the recommended root_namespace choice
Treats a blank response on root_namespace as accepting the shown default
Continues to the summary instead of asking a second root_namespace clarification question
Uses native structured inputs when available and a one-field-at-a-time plain-text fallback when they are not

evals.prompt: Create a new worker service named QueuePump using the dotnet-new-app-slnx skill.
evals.expected_output: A worker scaffold flow that preselects the Worker host type from the prompt and, when native input widgets are unavailable, falls back to a deterministic field-by-field plain-text sequence without extra conversational lead-ins before each field.
expectations: Preselects Worker from the prompt instead of asking the user to choose the host type again
Starts each plain-text fallback step with Field: <field-name> rather than a free-form chat preamble
Continues to collect only the remaining unresolved fields in FORMS order

evals.prompt: Scaffold a new worker service named TaglessWorker in a fresh folder before git init or adding any version tags.
evals.expected_output: A worker scaffold that keeps MinVer intact, warns that a bootstrap pre-release version such as 0.0.0-alpha.0 is expected until git is initialized and tagged, and does not replace MinVer with hardcoded version numbers.
expectations: Explains that MinVer bootstrap output in a non-git or untagged folder is expected initial state
Keeps MinVer wired into the scaffold instead of removing or bypassing it
Does not treat the expected MinVer bootstrap warning as a reason to inline package or app versions
